description: Python agent framework where everything is a tool: Agent = Engine + Tools + State, with Claude Code, Codex and provider APIs as swappable engines.
rules: Install with `pip install lazybridge` (Python 3.11+). Import core primitives from the top level: `from lazybridge import Agent, ClaudeCodeEngine, CodexEngine, Plan, Step, Memory, Store, Session`.
Construct agents as `Agent(name=..., engine=...)`. Model, system prompt, reasoning and native-tool policy go on the engine; `tools`, `output`, `verify`, memory/store/session go on the Agent.
Everything is a tool: pass plain typed callables, `Tool.wrap(fn, name=...)`, other named Agents or Plan-backed Agents in `tools=[...]`; do not write glue code to call one agent from another.
For writer/reviewer loops use `Agent(..., verify=reviewer_agent, max_verify=N)`; `verify` is a constructor option, not a run kwarg.
Read typed results from `result.payload` and text from `result.text()`; check `ok`/`error` on the Envelope before using it.

MCP, connectors and the async coding bridge live in LazyTools, not in LazyBridge. Install it from GitHub: `pip install "lazytoolkit[mcp] @ git+https://github.com/selvaz/LazyTools@v0.10.6"` and import from `lazytools`. Never `pip install lazytoolkit` from PyPI: that name is a placeholder.
Do not use legacy LazyAgent / LazyTool APIs or `lazybridge.ext.mcp`; they were removed. Follow docs/for-llms/codegen-contract.md and lazybridge/llms.json.
